purpose: Train a toxicity-scoring model without keeping personal data in clear.
legal_basis_note: Data minimisation (RGPD art. 5.1.c): identifiers removed before training.
source: Kaggle Jigsaw Toxic Comment Classification Challenge (public Wikipedia comments)

ner_labels_replaced.PERSON: Names identify natural persons directly (RGPD art. 4).
ner_labels_replaced.GPE: Cities, countries and regions can reveal where someone lives.
ner_labels_replaced.LOC: Other locations can reveal where someone lives or works.
ner_labels_replaced.FAC: Buildings and addresses can identify a person indirectly.

ner_labels_kept.NORP: Nationalities and religious or political groups are the target of toxic comments; removing them would destroy the signal the model must learn. They designate groups, not an identifiable individual.

limitations: NER is statistical: some names (misspelled, lowercase, nicknames) are missed.
Wikipedia usernames written without context are not detected.
Placeholders keep sentence structure, which is enough for toxicity scoring.
